_comment: The Model Tier Map (ADR-013). ENGINE.md and POLICIES.md speak only in tier names ('Fast tier', 'Capable tier') and never a vendor model identifier - this file is the ONE place that mapping lives, so porting to another engine means editing this file, not the specification. The engine can read this file but never write it (covered by the .harness/loop/** deny rule). Human-editable at install or port time.
_comment_effort: Each tier's effort level (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), passed as --effort. Until ADR-038 the engine read the operator's own settings and inherited their effortLevel; every run up to Kanso Run 7 ran at xhigh that way. Lowered to medium on 2026-10-13 by the human after Kanso Run 7, Iteration 3 took a five-hour window from 14% to 95% in 30 minutes. Delete the key to use the CLI default.

fast._comment: Worker dispatch by default (every task not classified Capable), and the top-level Iteration in its ordinary orchestrating capacity. NOT the Reviewer and NOT the Verifier.
fast._why_not_the_cheapest_model: This tier was 'haiku' for the Calendar-Note alarms run and fired exactly zero times: all 7 of 7 tasks were classified Capable and haiku consumed 6,363 input tokens and one cent across the whole run. A tier the planning roles are never willing to choose is not a tier, it is a comment. So the tier moved to a model a planner can actually pick for real Kotlin/Compose work. Since 2026-10-20 it is also the Worker default (POLICIES.md, Model Tier Criteria): the Kanso A/B run classified 4 of 5 tasks Capable and the Capable tier cost 76% of the run.

capable._comment: The Reviewer, the Verifier, the bootstrap Iteration that writes the plan, all bootstrap fan-out analysis roles (ADR-009), and any Worker whose task was classified Capable, or that escalated to this tier after a failed Fast-tier attempt.
